description: This Dryad release provides estimated 2018 traffic volumes by vehicle class on US public road segments and derived census-block traffic density. The authors began with Federal Highway Administration HPMS counts and trained random-forest regressions to estimate medium- and heavy-duty vehicle flows where truck counts were missing. The article reports coverage of 85.2 percent of public roadways across fifty states and Washington, DC. Dryad lists a large ZIP archive and README and states CC0 1.0. Coverage is a model-enhanced 2018 roadway network, not direct vehicle counts on every segment or hourly demand profiles. Regression uncertainty, sparse training coverage on lower-volume roads and census-block aggregation limit local exposure estimates. A reviewer-assessed simulation use is assigning class-specific traffic loads or air-pollution exposure surrogates to road-network scenarios. data-fhwa-hpms is the related source system, but its catalogue record does not explicitly name this derived Dryad release. The public Dryad page and file list were read; no ZIP or README payload was downloaded or model retrained.
